To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Azotobacter is a polyploid organism and this is the first report of the isolation of an essential gene mutant in this organism; (2) Azotobacters are able to sense iron levels and regulate expression of the essential phenylalanyl tRNA synthetase gene in response to iron availability; (3) the iron-regulated phenotype of pheST was not due to Fur binding to a DNA sequence in the promoter of pheS; and (4

1) the promoterless lux genes were used to create a reporter system for iron-regulated genes, 2) this system was used to show that the pheS and/or pheT genes are partially repressed by iron availability, and 3) the ferric uptake repressor (Fur) binds to the promoter of the pheS operon.
iron availability regulates pheS expression in Azotobacer, but the regulation does not appear to involve the ferric uptake regulator Fur.
In summary, our research is concerned with
iron regulation of the pheS and fur genes in Azotobacteria.
understanding the role of the Fur repressor in regulating gene expression in response to changes in iron availability.
the identification and characterization of a new iron-regulated gene, pheS, and the identification of a novel regulatory system in A. vinelndii.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the iron-repressible promoterless luxAB transgene was localized to a chromosomal region encoding the pheS and the pheT genes and that the PHES::lux reporter activity was partially iron-repressible.
the pheS promoter is iron-regulated in Azotobacer vinelandii.
iron regulates pheST expression in A. vinlandii.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pheT gene is essential in A. vinlandii, that there is iron-dependent regulation of the pheST operon, and that the iron-regulatory Fur protein is not the mediator of this regulation.
the pheST genes are partially regulated by iron availability in Azotobacters, but the mechanism is not known.
Azotobacter pheT and pheS are both regulated by iron availability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
iron availability is a major regulator of protein biosynthetic pathways.
the pheT gene is essential for growth of A. vinelandiii.
the pheST operon is partially repressed under high-iron conditions and fully derepresses in response to iron limitation.
